## Inputs and revision

This example replaces a complete document without overwriting a newer update.
Read retrieves the stored document and its revision, a version number.
Edit prepares a complete replacement using that revision as expectedRevision.
Let $r$ be the stored revision; an accepted replacement increments it:

$$
r_{next} = r + 1
$$

```typescript
const update = {
  documentId: "4e7efb70-6686-4f94-aa51-f97d40abb677",
  expectedRevision: 3,
  document: completeDocument,
};
```

slides.title: Success and conflict
slides.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  Read["Read"] --> Edit["Edit"]
  Edit --> Validate["Validate"]
  Validate --> Compare{"Revision?"}
  Compare -->|Match| Commit["Commit"]
  Compare -->|Stale| Conflict["Conflict"]
  Conflict --> Read
  Commit --> Result["Saved"]
slides.explanationMarkdown:
Validate checks structure and content policy.
Revision? compares the supplied revision with the stored revision.
A match permits Commit to persist the replacement and Saved to return its new revision.
Conflict makes no write and returns to Read so a newer update is not lost.

slides.title: Prepare the input
slides.explanationMarkdown:
Read provides both the content and revision needed by Edit.
Keep block and slide IDs stable where the content has the same role.
Send the complete edited document, not a patch.

slides.title: Check and commit
slides.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  Edit["Edit"] --> Validate["Validate"]
  Validate --> Compare{"Revision?"}
  Compare -->|Match| Commit["Commit"]
  Compare -->|Stale| Conflict["Conflict"]
  Conflict --> Read["Read"]

slides.title: Saved result
slides.explanationMarkdown:
Commit completes persistence before Saved reports the new revision.
This result does not verify Mermaid, math, readability, or content correctness.

blocks.markdown:
## Failure boundary

Validation errors and revision conflicts leave the stored document unchanged.
The recovery path below preserves another writer's changes instead of resubmitting stale content.

slides.title: Reapply the intended change
slides.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  Conflict["Conflict"] --> Read["Read"]
  Read --> Edit["Edit"]
slides.explanationMarkdown:
Read obtains the new stored version.
Edit reapplies the intended change while retaining unrelated updates and uses the new revision.
Do not discard another writer's change without an explicit decision.

blocks.markdown:
## Conclusion

A replacement succeeds only after validation, a matching revision, and commit.
On conflict, read again and reapply the intended change.
After saving, open the viewer and check the full article and every slide at desktop and 390px, or report the missing coverage as unverified.
Keep rendering, readability, source correctness, and human acceptance separate from storage success.
